newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Ringgit falls back on interbank dollar bids.
newsitem.headline: Ringgit falls back on interbank dollar bids.

text.p: The ringgit fell back to around opening levels in late Asian trading on short-covering and persistent dollar bids by interbank players, dealers said.
The ringgit had firmed in early trading following reports of comments by acting Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim that the spillover effects from the Thai baht would be temporary.

Anwar, who is also finance minister, was quoted by Malaysian newspapers as saying the economic fundamentals in Malaysia and Thailand were different and thus, the ringgit should not be severely affected by the baht-crisis.

"The reports sparked off commercial and offshore selling of dollar/ringgit from 2.5150 to 2.5110 this morning," said a dealer with a European bank in Kuala Lumpur. But profit-taking and interbank bids pushed the dollar back up again, he said.
Dealers said some selling in ringgit/Singapore dollar cross aided the dollar rebound.
The dollar/ringgit was expected to continue trading in the 2.5050-2.5200 range in the near term, they said.
At 0930 GMT, the ringgit was quoted at 2.5150/60 a dollar against 2.5160/65 at close in Kuala Lumpur on Thursday.
